intro:
The fifteen London components are built on the real London page. The side-by-side shows each one
beside the canvas frame you picked, at 375, 768 and 1280px:
https://claude.ai/artifact/EPtLABruWw8yjBwFj5skf6. Each card says what differs on purpose.
Question 1 is the confirmation Plan 2 waits on; the rest are decisions the build could not make
for you. Claude's recommendation is marked.

questions.context: Every difference that is on purpose is written on its card: - a different served photo where the canvas repeated Maggie's; - bold headings; - the capped type sizes you asked for on 2026-09-28; - the column beside the dial; - no guarantee line; - the review in three paragraphs. If any component differs in a way you do not want, name it and what to change. It is fixed in that component and the side-by-side is republished at the same link.

options.label: Some differ; I name them in the text box

questions.question: Do the fifteen built components match the canvas picks?
questions.where: Plan 2 closes (Task 11) on your yes; then the London page run starts with its research board.

questions.context: A served photo may appear once per page (its alt text stays word for word, and a repeated alt fails the image gate), so where the canvas used Maggie's photo five times the page uses: - Jones's portrait (trust strip); - Jones seated (takeaways); - Byrd (chapter one); - the London owner photo (FAQ rail). Maggie stays on the puppy sheet. Recommended: (a) — every photo is one the site already serves and ranks, so nothing new is added. Trade-off: the canvas's Maggie-first look is softer on those four components.

options.label: Use other served photos; I name them in the text box

questions.question: Keep the photo swaps?
questions.where: the London page board's image slots; any file named there is accepted.

questions.context: The header is shared with the 12 built pages; the band is your pick. Recommended: (b) — it frees the screen on the city pages only and leaves the 12 built pages untouched. Trade-off: the band's step numbers are hidden while the reader scrolls down.

options.label: The jump band slides away while scrolling down and comes back on scrolling up
The band shrinks to one slim row after the first scroll

questions.question: On a phone, the site header plus the jump band cover about 27% of the screen (221 of 812px at 375).

questions.context: From 640 to 839px the puppy count sits above the price line so the four prices keep their width. Placed on the line, as the canvas has it, "£1,700" ran up to 21px outside its panel. Recommended: (a) — it is the only layout measured to fit at every width from 640 to 1100px. Trade-off: at those widths it differs from the canvas.

options.label: Keep the count above the line from 640 to 839px
Try a smaller price size in that range instead

questions.question: Keep the price scale's tablet layout?

questions.context: Beside the dial, the contents list repeats the same sections. The site's other pages hide their contents list from 1024px; your London pick shows it at every width. Recommended: (a) — it is your pick as designed. Trade-off: the section names appear twice on a desktop screen.

options.label: Show it at every width (as picked)
Hide it from 1024px, as the other pages do

questions.question: Show the contents list at desktop too?

questions.context: Its heading sits in a narrow column beside the answers, as on the canvas. The other headings now wrap to two lines at most on desktop. Recommended: (b) — it matches the "no tall headers" ruling. Trade-off: the answers column gets narrower.

options.label: Keep it as on the canvas
Give the heading column more width so it wraps to two lines

questions.question: The takeaways heading wraps to three lines on desktop.

questions.context: The canvas said "two-year health guarantee", but no page may state a length until you give one (`guarantee_days` is empty), so every guarantee line is hidden today. If you give it, the trust strip, takeaways and FAQ print it from the data.

options.label: Another length; I give it in the text box
Leave it off the site for now

questions.question: How long is the health guarantee?

questions.context: You said the puppies are now 10 weeks old, but the data has no birth date. With one, every page can work their age out and never go stale.
questions.question: What is the litter's date of birth?

title: London side-by-side · confirm the match and seven decisions
